text:
Connor O'Brien: hey folks — trying to map the upcoming model changelog work to our runtime release trains. how do you see “model version notes” aligning w/ runtime releases? esp around freeze windows

Connor O'Brien: constraints on my side:
- we run weekly train (Mon cut, Wed/Thu deploy)
- freeze window Thu 5pm PT -> Mon 9am PT (no customer-facing changes unless exception)
- runtime RCs start Tue; we try not to introduce new publish pipelines during RC

Connor O'Brien: if the generator publishes to docs/console independently of runtime deploy, that’s effectively a second release train. is that intended?

ReleaseBot: :wave: Reminder: if this impacts train process, please capture in release-notes-policy doc. (automated)

Dylan Brooks: good q. we were *intending* changelog to be driven by model-registry change events, not tied 1:1 to runtime builds. but we should define how it behaves during freeze.

Dylan Brooks: +1 that it’s basically a separate pipeline. the “customer-visible” part is gated by approval status (draft -> in_review -> published). that might give you the control you need.

Connor O'Brien: ok but even “publish” is a production change (docs + console data) and can confuse customers if it lands mid-freeze. can we guarantee we don’t publish during freeze unless explicit override?

Michael Nguyen: generator can be configured to queue events + generate drafts but not push to publish targets until a “publish window” opens.

Michael Nguyen: thought: two knobs
1) ingestion (always on)
2) publication (blocked during freeze; can be overridden w/ a break-glass flag)

Ethan Park: fwiw control plane endpoints can serve drafts only to internal users; published entries only go to external feeds/console.

Ethan Park: so during freeze, we could still let internal folks review drafts and be ready to hit publish once freeze lifts.

Connor O'Brien: that helps. what about cases where runtime release changes performance for specific models (kernel swap, batching changes). do we create model changelog entries for that too?

Dylan Brooks: my preference: yes, but only if it’s customer-impacting and model-specific. the entry would reference runtime version and link to runtime notes.

Jada Williams: workflow-wise we can add a “related_runtime_release” field on the changelog entry metadata (not necessarily in the model metadata schema itself). then templates can show a line like “Also included in Runtime 2024.02.1”.

Connor O'Brien: cool. but we need to avoid a situation where runtime deploy hits Thu and the model changelog publishes Fri during freeze because an event fired.

Michael Nguyen: we can enforce publish policy in the generator service itself (checks freeze calendar) AND in the publish endpoint (server-side guard). defense in depth.

Logan Wright: from observability side: we should expose a metric for “drafts awaiting publish due to freeze” so release doesn’t get surprised Mon morning.

Logan Wright: something like `changelog.publish_blocked_count` + `oldest_blocked_age_hours`.

Connor O'Brien: nice. who owns updating the freeze calendar / config? release eng doesn’t want to be the only ones holding the keys for a product feature.

Dylan Brooks: we can wire it to the same config source we use for feature flag windows (control plane config). release eng can be an approver, not the only operator.

Elliot Price: docs perspective: publishing to docs site is a deploy job too (content sync). during freeze we also try not to change nav/content unless required.

Elliot Price: if generator is writing to a feed that the docs site consumes, that’s still “customer-facing change” even if no docs deploy happens.

Connor O'Brien: yeah exactly — even if it’s “just data”, customers will see it.

Michael Nguyen: ack. then our policy should treat feed updates as customer-facing publish. freeze guard applies there too.

Jada Williams: we can also add a “scheduled_publish_at” option per entry. e.g. you approve it mid-week and schedule it for Mon 9:05am PT.

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: that’s a good compromise. keeps us from rushing during RC.

Connor O'Brien: action items?
1) document: model changelog publish is its own pipeline but must respect release freeze
2) implement: publish guard + break-glass override (audited)
3) define: when runtime-only changes warrant a model changelog entry (rule of thumb)

Dylan Brooks: +1. Michael can you add a note in the generator tech plan about freeze-aware publishing + scheduling? Connor I’ll sync w/ you on what goes in the release policy doc.

Michael Nguyen: yep will add. will propose default: no external publish Thu 5pm -> Mon 9am PT, unless `release_exception=true` and approval from Release Eng + Product.

Connor O'Brien: perfect. also pls make sure the exception path leaves an audit trail (who/when/why). enterprise customers *will* ask.

Ethan Park: can route exceptions through the publish endpoint w/ required “reason” field. audit log can capture actor + reason + entry_id.

Connor O'Brien: great. thanks all — this gives me enough to update train docs + set expectations with PM.

Dylan Brooks: :+1: I’ll follow up w/ a short writeup so we don’t lose the decisions.
